title: Foundation Models for Generalist Robot Learning: Cross-Embodiment Data, Language-Conditioned Visuomotor Policies, and Scalable Skill Transfer
background:
Recent advances in foundation models have catalyzed a paradigm shift in robot learning, moving from task-specific controllers toward generalist policies trained on heterogeneous, large-scale interaction data. The Open X-Embodiment initiative aggregated trajectories across 22+ robot platforms, enabling RT-X policies that demonstrate positive transfer across morphologies [1]. Vision-language-action (VLA) models such as RT-2 and OpenVLA further showed that internet-scale vision-language pretraining can be co-finetuned with robot trajectories to yield language-conditioned manipulation policies with emergent semantic generalization [2][3]. In parallel, diffusion-based action heads and flow-matching decoders have improved multi-modal action prediction under noisy human teleoperation data [4], while autonomous data flywheels using scripted resets and DAgger-style relabeling have begun to scale data collection beyond human demonstrations [5].

Despite this progress, several fundamental gaps prevent robust deployment. First, cross-embodiment transfer remains brittle: action spaces, kinematics, and observation viewpoints differ across platforms, and current models rely on per-embodiment tokenizers or dataset-mixture heuristics that do not generalize zero-shot to unseen robots [1][3]. Second, language grounding is shallow: VLAs frequently fail on compositional instructions, spatial relations, and long-horizon tasks requiring temporal abstraction [2][6]. Third, data scaling laws for robotics are poorly understood — unlike text, robot data is expensive, non-i.i.d., and dominated by short-horizon pick-and-place, leaving open how to allocate collection budgets across embodiments, scenes, and skills. Finally, real-world evaluation remains under-standardized, and safety guarantees for foundation-model-driven controllers operating under distribution shift are largely absent.
challenges: Designing embodiment-agnostic action representations (e.g., unified latent action spaces or morphology-conditioned decoders) that enable zero-shot transfer to robots with unseen kinematics, end-effectors, and control frequencies, without per-platform finetuning

Closing the language-grounding gap for compositional, spatially-referential, and long-horizon instructions, including hierarchical decomposition between high-level VLM planners and low-level visuomotor policies with consistent semantic interfaces

Establishing empirical scaling laws for robot foundation models that quantify the marginal value of additional embodiments, scenes, skills, and demonstration quality, and using these to design cost-optimal autonomous data collection pipelines

Achieving sample-efficient real-world adaptation under distribution shift (novel objects, lighting, dynamics) while preserving pretrained capabilities, including mechanisms to detect out-of-distribution states and defer or request human intervention

Developing reproducible, contamination-free evaluation protocols and safety certificates for language-conditioned policies, covering both simulated benchmarks and standardized physical task suites across labs
